visible_symptoms: faint yellow vein clearing along the midrib and lateral veins; slight upward waviness at the leaf tip margin; leaf blade otherwise predominantly green; small reddish mark at the petiole junction
caption_1: Faint yellow tracing along the main veins. Tip edge slightly wavy. No other discoloration visible.
caption_2: The leaf tip curls upward just slightly, barely enough to notice unless you're looking for it.
caption_3: Hard to tell much is wrong here — just some pale lines tracking the veins.
caption_4: Strip out the vein tracing and you're left with a leaf that reads as clean.
caption_5: Held between two fingers with a stretch of dirt and green blurred out behind it, the leaf's only flaw is the faint yellow lines running along its veins.

visible_symptoms: both side lobes curl/cup upward, leaving the leaf non-flat; fine dark stippling across the leaf surface; faint pale tracing along the main veins
caption_1: Both lobes curled inward. Surface dotted with fine dark specks.
caption_2: The blade doesn't sit flat — it dips toward the center where the lobes pull up on either side.
caption_3: This one's definitely cupped, not flat like it should be.
caption_4: Where an unaffected leaf would lie flat in your hand, this one bows upward at both edges.
caption_5: Pinched at the stem between thumb and finger, the blade keeps its upward curl even from this angle, and a faint yellow line still traces each main vein beneath the speckling.

visible_symptoms: extensive magenta/crimson patches between major veins; yellow chlorotic halo ringing the red patches; dark brownish-purple necrotic speckling inside several red patches; veins remain green while surrounding tissue is discolored; leaf margin tinged red-brown
caption_1: Deep red-pink blotches between most veins. Yellow rims around each one. A few centers gone dark and gritty.
caption_2: The discoloration follows the spaces between major veins almost exactly, like it's tracing the leaf's own architecture.
caption_3: This leaf's seen better days — barely any plain green left on it.
caption_4: A few patches near the margin have gone past red into a darker, almost burnt color.
caption_5: Pink and magenta spread across nearly every section of the blade, each patch ringed in yellow; the veins themselves keep their normal green color running straight through the damage.

visible_symptoms: irregular pale cream/white blotches across multiple lobes; one lobe almost entirely white; blotch borders cut across veins rather than following them; reddish petiole base visible
caption_1: Right lobe: nearly all white. Middle lobe: pale, green only along the veins. Left lobe: mixed green and cream.
caption_2: The cream patches cut straight across the veins in several spots, ignoring them completely.
caption_3: One side of this leaf has basically lost its color.
caption_4: Out in the same patch of soil, the neighboring leaves are a normal solid green — this one clearly isn't.
caption_5: Still rooted in the soil with grass pressing in around it, the leaf splits unevenly into a near-white lobe, a half-pale one, and a third that's only lightly mottled.

visible_symptoms: one lobe nearly all white/cream; middle lobe partly pale; third lobe more mottled with green dominant; irregular cream patches not bound by veins
caption_1: Three lobes. Right one cream-colored. Middle half pale. Left mostly green with light spotting.
caption_2: Pale sectors spread unevenly, heaviest toward the tip of the right lobe and fading out toward the base.
caption_3: From above, you can see exactly where the color starts dropping out.
caption_4: A small bud nearby in the soil furrow is a plain green, nothing like the lobe right above it.
caption_5: Looking down at the plant, the narrow right lobe reads almost paper-white next to the darker soil furrow beside it; the other two lobes keep more of their green.

visible_symptoms: two small grayish-brown necrotic blotches near the upper-right area; irregular lesion edges; remainder of the leaflet uniformly green
caption_1: Two gray-brown spots, upper right. Nothing else visible.
caption_2: Both lesions have ragged, uneven edges rather than a clean circular shape.
caption_3: Just a couple of small marks — easy to miss if you weren't looking closely.
caption_4: Two blotches are the whole story here — everything else on the leaflet is plain green.
caption_5: Photographed on a plain gray background, the leaflet's green is broken only at one corner, where two small lesions sit close together.

visible_symptoms: one central grayish-brown lesion mid-leaf; tiny additional dark speck lower-right; slightly rugose leaf surface with prominent veins; remainder of leaflet green
caption_1: One lesion, just above the midrib. Small dark fleck lower right.
caption_2: The surface has a slightly wrinkled texture, with veins standing out more than usual.
caption_3: Not much going on here besides that one gray patch.
caption_4: One gray mark above the midrib, one tiny fleck below — that's the entire list of complaints.
caption_5: The leaflet's texture looks slightly puckered around the main veins, almost rippled, with just one lesion interrupting the green elsewhere on the blade.

visible_symptoms: larger tan-brown lesion at the lower tip reaching the leaf margin; darker brown/black specks embedded within the lesion; couple of tiny additional dark dots elsewhere; remainder of leaflet glossy green
caption_1: Large tan-brown lesion at the tip. Dark flecks inside it. A couple of tiny dots elsewhere.
caption_2: The lesion reaches all the way to the leaf edge, where the tissue looks dried rather than just discolored.
caption_3: This one's worse than the other two potato leaflets — bigger damage, darker center.
caption_4: This lesion is in a different league entirely than a leaflet carrying just one or two pinprick marks.
caption_5: The leaflet keeps a glossy shine across nearly all of it, but the lower tip has dried into a brown patch flecked with darker specks, right where the blade comes to a point.

visible_symptoms: yellow chlorotic mottling across the left/lower-left half of the leaflet; slightly fuzzy texture within the affected zone; right half remains green; serrated leaf margin intact
caption_1: Left half: dull yellow. Right half: green. Split is roughly down the middle.
caption_2: The serrated edge stays intact on both sides — only the color changes.
caption_3: Half of this leaflet just isn't green anymore.
caption_4: The line between yellow and green here is sharper than you'd expect — almost a clean cut down the middle of the leaflet.
caption_5: There's a faint fuzziness to the yellowed patch that you don't feel on the green side, like the texture itself has changed along with the color.

visible_symptoms: subtle yellow speckling near the center-right close to the midrib; remainder of leaflet mostly green; short petiole visible
caption_1: Light yellow speckling, just right of the midrib. Everything else green.
caption_2: The leaflet's pointed tip and serrated edge are both undisturbed — the only change is in color.
caption_3: You'd probably walk past this one without noticing anything.
caption_4: Out of the four tomato leaflets in this set, this is the lightest case by a clear margin.
caption_5: With its short stem intact, the leaflet lies flat on a neutral gray surface, and the faint mottling near the midrib only becomes obvious up close.

visible_symptoms: faint pale/tan blotching near the mid-left margin; remainder of leaflet dark green and glossy
caption_1: One faded patch, left margin. Dark green everywhere else.
caption_2: The lobed shape of the leaflet is clean and undistorted — no curling, no folding.
caption_3: Barely anything to flag on this one.
caption_4: This is about as mild as the mold gets in this group of tomato leaflets.
caption_5: A tiny dark speck floats on the gray background near the leaflet's edge — just debris, not a symptom; the leaf itself stays dark green and glossy except for one faded patch.

visible_symptoms: sharp yellow chlorotic patch covering the upper-right lobe; lower-left lobes remain green; slightly textured/fuzzy yellowed area; small petiole and stem visible
caption_1: Upper-right lobe: yellow. Lower lobes: green. Sharp line between them.
caption_2: Each of the three lobes in this little cluster is doing something different color-wise.
caption_3: One lobe is a completely different color from the other two.
caption_4: The lower two lobes match the green you'd expect on a healthy tomato plant; the top one clearly doesn't.
caption_5: The yellowed lobe has a slightly rougher feel to it than the smooth green ones below, like the surface itself thickened along with the color shift.

visible_symptoms: small tan-brown raised spots along the upper-right margin and near the midrib; lower half of the leaf clean; remainder dark glossy green
caption_1: A handful of small brown spots, upper right and near the midrib. Lower half clean.
caption_2: Each spot sits just slightly raised, not flush with the blade surface.
caption_3: Pretty minor, honestly — nearly all of this leaf is still its normal dark green.
caption_4: No spotting anywhere near the lower half — whatever's affecting this leaf so far is staying near the top.
caption_5: The leaf's deep green barely changes anywhere except for a scatter of small lesions clustered toward the upper right and along the midrib.

visible_symptoms: overall yellow-green chlorosis across the whole leaf; scattered small dark brown/black speckled spots lower-center; one larger tan blotch near the center; small notch missing from the margin (likely incidental, not disease-related)
caption_1: Whole leaf: pale yellow-green. Dark speckles lower-center. One bigger tan blotch near the middle.
caption_2: There's a notch missing from the right edge — probably an insect bite, not part of the infection.
caption_3: This is the roughest-looking pepper leaf in the set, no question.
caption_4: A pepper leaf this color wouldn't be mistaken for a healthy one from across a field.
caption_5: Pale yellow-green has taken over what should be a darker leaf, and a loose scatter of dark spots, including one larger tan patch, sits in the lower-middle area.

visible_symptoms: overall yellow-green leaf color; darker brown/black necrotic patches along the upper-left and lower-left margins; scattered tiny dark specks across the surface; margin slightly curled and dried near the necrotic patches
caption_1: Yellow-green overall. Dark necrotic patches, top-left and bottom-left. Tiny specks scattered between.
caption_2: The margin curls slightly and looks dried right where the darker patches sit.
caption_3: Color's gone wrong on basically this whole leaf.
caption_4: Brown-black necrosis at two edges, lighter speckling everywhere between — this leaf is past the point of looking like simple spotting.
caption_5: Necrotic brown-black patches sit at both the upper-left and lower-left edges, with finer dark specks scattered more thinly elsewhere on the blade.

visible_symptoms: mostly healthy dark green glossy leaf; small brown lesions concentrated near the upper-left margin; one tiny dark mark near the lower-right edge
caption_1: A few brown marks near the upper-left edge. One tiny mark lower right. Green everywhere else.
caption_2: The leaf keeps its rounded shape and glossy finish without any curling or distortion.
caption_3: Among the pepper leaves here, this one's barely touched.
caption_4: The more advanced cases in this batch make this one look like nothing happened at all.
caption_5: Deep green and glossy across the blade, with just a few small lesions tucked near the top edge and a single dark mark down by the opposite corner.
